overview.title: cyOverview
overview.description1: cyThis privacy policy explains why we collect your personal data, what we do with it, and your rights. More information about using this service is in the <a routerlink="/terms-and-conditions" href="/terms-and-conditions" >terms and conditions</a >.

whoManagesThisService.title: cyWho manages this service
whoManagesThisService.description1: cyThis service is managed by Her Majesty’s Courts and Tribunals Service (HMCTS) and we’re responsible for protecting the personal data you provide.
whoManagesThisService.description2: cyHMCTS is an executive agency of the Ministry of Justice (MoJ). The MoJ is the data controller and their <a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/ministry-of-justice/about/personal-information-charter" >personal information charter</a > explains more about how they process personal data.
whoManagesThisService.description3: cyWhen you use this service we (HMCTS) will ask you to provide some personal data.

whyWeCollectYourPersonalData.title: cyWhy we collect your personal data
whyWeCollectYourPersonalData.description1: cyWe collect your personal data to:
whyWeCollectYourPersonalData.description2: cyOur staff use your personal data to process your claim or application. They work in the UK and your data is stored in the UK.

typesOfPersonalDataWeCollect.title: cyTypes of personal data we collect
typesOfPersonalDataWeCollect.description1: cyThe personal data we collect includes:
typesOfPersonalDataWeCollect.description2: cySome services collect more personal data. Find out more about the <a routerlink="/privacy-policy" fragment="otherservices" href="/privacy-policy#otherservices" >personal data that is collected by the service you are using</a >.

list.item1: cyyour name, address and contact details
list.item2: cyyour email and password (if you create an account)
list.item3: cyother personal information you provide in your claim or application

usingYourData.title: cyUsing your data
usingYourData.description1: cyAs part of your claim you’ll be asked to use your email address to set up an account. You will be able to use this email and password to sign into other HMCTS services.
usingYourData.description2: cyWe may ask for your permission to use your email address to send you emails using GOV.UK Notify. This system processes emails only within the European Economic Area until the point where emails are handed over to the email provider you use.
usingYourData.description3: cyWe use your personal information in connection with the provision of the IdAM Service. In particular, your personal information may be used for the following purposes:

list.item1: cyCommunicate with you and other individuals.
list.item2: cyMake assessments and decisions about your identity to manage your access to Services on the Common Platform and maintain information security.
list.item3: cyImprove the quality of the IdAM Service.
list.item4: cyPrevent, detect and investigate crime, including fraud.
list.item6: cyPersonalise your experience when you use the IdAM Service.
list.item7: cyManage our operations and IT infrastructure, in line with our internal policies and procedures, including those relating to IT systems operation; data and platform hosting; data analytics; business continuity; and records management.
list.item8: cyManage complaints, feedback and queries, and handle requests for data access or correction, or the exercise of other rights relating to personal information.
list.item9: cyComply with applicable laws and regulatory obligations (including those outside your country of residence); comply with legal process and court orders; and respond to requests from public and other government authorities (including those outside your country of residence).
list.item10: cyEstablish and defend legal rights to protect our operations and secure our and your rights, privacy, safety or property, and those of other individuals or third parties; to enforce our terms and conditions; and pursue available remedies or limit our damages.

storingYourData.title: cyStoring your data
storingYourData.description1: cyWhen you make your claim or application we store the data you have provided. The amount of time that your data is kept for depends on the service that you are using.
storingYourData.description2: cyWhen you make your claim or application we store the data you have provided. The amount of time that your data is kept for depends on the service that you are using.
storingYourData.description3: cySome services collect more personal data. Find out more about the <a routerlink="/privacy-policy" fragment="otherservices" href="/privacy-policy#otherservices" >personal data that is collected by the service you are using</a >.

sharingYourData.title: cySharing your data
sharingYourData.description1: cyWhile processing your claim or application, another government department, agency or organisation might be involved and we may share your data with them.
sharingYourData.description2: cyIf you contact us and ask for help with the service you are using, your personal data may be shared with the Good Things Foundation. This is a company who we have partnered with to offer face to face support.
sharingYourData.description3: cyIn some circumstances we may share your data for example, to prevent or detect crime, or to produce anonymised statistics.
sharingYourData.description4: cyWe use Google Analytics to collect data about how a website is used. This anonymous data is shared with Google. Find out about this in our terms and conditions.

storingAndSharingYourDataInternationally.title: cyStoring and sharing your data internationally
storingAndSharingYourDataInternationally.description1: cySometimes we need to send your personal information outside of the UK. When we do this we comply with data protection law.

list1.item1: cyto see the personal data that we hold on you
list1.item2: cyto have the personal data corrected
list1.item3: cyto have the personal data removed or deleted (this will depend on the circumstances, for example if you decide not to continue your claim or application)
list1.item4: cythat access to the personal data is restricted (for example, you can ask to have your data stored for longer and not automatically deleted)

yourRights.description2: cyIf you want to see the personal data that we hold on you, you can:

list2.item2: cywrite to us: Data Protection Team, Ministry of Justice, 11th Floor, Post Point 11.52, 102 Petty France, London SW1H 9AJ

yourRights.description3: cyYou can ask for more information about:

list3.item1: cyagreements we have on sharing information with other organisations
list3.item2: cywhen we are allowed to pass on personal information without telling you
list3.item3: cyour instructions to staff on how to collect, use or delete your personal information
list3.item4: cyour instructions to staff on how to collect, use or delete your personal information

yourRights.description4: cyYou can contact the MoJ data protection officer, by:

list4.item1: cyhow we check that the information we hold is accurate and up-to-date

howToComplain.title: cyHow to complain
howToComplain.description1: cySee our <a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/hm-courts-and-tribunals-service/about/complaints-procedure" >complaints procedure</a > if you want to complain about how we've handled your personal data.
howToComplain.description2: cyWrite to: Data Protection Team, Ministry of Justice, 11th Floor, Post Point 11.52, 102 Petty France, London SW1H 9AJ
howToComplain.description4: cyYou can also complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office if you’re not satisfied with our response or believe we are not processing your personal data lawfully.

usingTheApplyForADivorceService.title: cyUsing the apply for a divorce service

thePersonalDataWeNeed.title: cyThe personal data we need
thePersonalDataWeNeed.description1: cyWhen you use the apply for divorce service we need the following personal data:

list.item2: cyyour name on the marriage certificate
list.item3: cya copy of your marriage certificate
list.item5: cycountry in which you got married
list.item6: cyinformation about where you have lived
list.item7: cyyour habitual residence (whether your life is mainly based in England or Wales)
list.item8: cyyour domicile (usually the place in which you were born, regard as your permanent home and to which you have the closest ties)
list.item9: cyyour email or mobile phone number
list.item12: cyto know if you have been involved in other court cases
list.item13: cyyour husband or wife’s current name
list.item14: cytheir name on the marriage certificate
list.item15: cythe name and address of the person who committed adultery with your husband or wife (this is optional and only asked if adultery is your reason for divorce)
list.item16: cyyour solicitors name and address (if you have one)

receivingNotifications.title: cyReceiving notifications
receivingNotifications.description1: cyYou need to sign up to receive notifications to use the apply for divorce service. This is a legal requirement so that the divorce application can proceed.

storingYourData2.title: cyStoring your data
storingYourData2.description1: cyWhen you use this service you’ll be asked to use your email address to set up an account. You will be able to use this email and password to sign into other HMCTS services.
storingYourData2.description2: cyWhile you are filling out or responding to a divorce application we will hold your data for up to 6 months. If you don’t complete the application during this time you’ll have to start again.
storingYourData2.description3: cyWhen a divorce is finalised the case is stored for 18 years. After this time, some data (from the decree nisi and the decree absolute) is deleted.
storingYourData2.description4: cyThe remainder of the case information is stored for an additional 82 years. After a total of 100 years this data will be deleted.

sharingYourData2.title: cySharing your data
sharingYourData2.description1: cyWhile processing your claim or application, another government department, agency or organisation might be involved and we may share your data with them.
sharingYourData2.description2: cyAny data you provide which needs to be printed will be shared with Xerox (UK) Ltd. For example, the divorce application will be printed so that it can be sent to the respondent by post.
sharingYourData2.description3: cyAny data which is posted in to support a divorce application will be shared with Exela Technologies Limited. For example, a posted marriage certificate will be received by Exela and sent to the court as a scanned image.
sharingYourData2.description4: cyIf you contact us and ask for help with the service you're using, your personal data may be shared with the Good Things Foundation. This is a company who we have partnered with to offer face to face support.
sharingYourData2.description5: cyIn some circumstances we may share your data for example, to prevent or detect crime, or to produce anonymised statistics.

thePersonalDataWeNeed2.title: cyThe personal data we need
thePersonalDataWeNeed2.description1: cyIf you are using the money claims service we will ask you for:

list1.item2: cyyour business or organisation if you are acting on their behalf
list1.item4: cyyour email or mobile phone number
list1.item6: cythe name of the person, business or organisation you are claiming against
list1.item9: cythe reasons you are making the claim
list1.item10: cythe timeline of events leading to the dispute
list1.item11: cya list of any evidence you have to support your claim

thePersonalDataWeNeed2.description2: cyIf you are responding to a money claim we ask you to check the personal information about you that was provided by the claimant which includes your name, your address and contact details.
thePersonalDataWeNeed2.description3: cyWe may ask you to provide:

list2.item2: cyyour business or organisation if you are acting on their behalf
list2.item3: cyyour response to the claim made against you
list2.item4: cythe timeline of events leading to the dispute
list2.item5: cya list of any evidence you have to support your claim

storingYourData3.title: cyStoring your data
storingYourData3.description1: cyWhen you use this service you’ll be asked to use your email address to set up an account. You can use this email and password to sign into other HMCTS services.

beforeYouSubmitYourInformation.title: cyBefore you submit your information
beforeYouSubmitYourInformation.description1: cyThe information you enter in the money claims service is saved until you decide to submit it. This allows you to save what you are doing and continue later. Saved information that you do not submit will be deleted after 90 days.

afterYouSubmitYourInformation.title: cyAfter you submit your information
afterYouSubmitYourInformation.description1: cyThe information you submit for a money claim will be deleted 2 years after the court makes a decision on the outcome of your claim (this is called a judgment).
afterYouSubmitYourInformation.description2: cyIf the court doesn’t make a decision about your claim (for example, you settle the claim out of court and a judgment is no longer required) then the information you provide will be deleted 3 years after the last update made to the claim.

sharingYourData3.title: cySharing your data
sharingYourData3.description1: cyThe information you submit will be shared with everyone who is named on the claim. This excludes any payment details that you use to pay court fees.
sharingYourData3.description2: cyIf a judgment is made on a case some information is shared with Registry Trust Limited who provide financial information about court judgments to banks and credit agencies.
sharingYourData3.description3: cyAny data posted in by you or other parties to support the claim issue and progression will be shared with Exela Technologies Limited and, if printing is required, with Xerox (UK) Ltd.

usingTheAppealABenefitDecisionService.title: cyUsing the appeal a benefit decision service

thePersonalDataWeNeed3.title: cyThe personal data we need
thePersonalDataWeNeed3.description1: cyWhen you use the appeal a benefit decision service we ask for:

list1.item3: cyyour email or mobile phone number
list1.item5: cyinformation from the Mandatory Reconsideration Notice
list1.item6: cyinformation on any support you need for a hearing, if you attend one
list1.item7: cyinformation on your availability for a hearing, if you attend one

thePersonalDataWeNeed3.description2: cyIf you have a representative, we will ask for:
thePersonalDataWeNeed3.description3: cyIf you are appointee, you will need to provide information about the person who you are appealing on behalf of, including:

receivingNotifications2.title: cyReceiving notifications
receivingNotifications2.description1: cyAs part of your appeal we’ll ask if you want to receive text message and email notifications to keep you updated with your appeal.
receivingNotifications2.description2: cyYou can cancel text messages by following the steps mentioned in the text message, and you can cancel emails by following the steps mentioned in the emails.
receivingNotifications2.description3: cyIf you have asked for your named representative to receive updates on your appeal, then we will share your data with them. If you want your representative to stop receiving notifications then you need to Contact us.

storingAndSharingYourData.title: cyStoring and sharing your data
storingAndSharingYourData.description1: cyYour data will be shared with the government department that made the decision you are appealing against. For example, the Department for Work and Pensions or HM Revenue and Customs. This is so that department can respond to your appeal.
storingAndSharingYourData.description2: cyAfter you complete your application it will be stored for 2 years. It will be deleted after that.

usingTheApplyForProbateService.title: cyUsing the apply for probate service

thePersonalDataWeCollect.title: cyThe personal data we collect
thePersonalDataWeCollect.description1: cyWhen you use the apply for probate service we ask for:

list.item1: cyyour name, and any other names you are known as
list.item5: cythe names of any executors of the will
list.item6: cycontact details for all of the executors who are applying for probate

storingYourData4.title: cyStoring your data
storingYourData4.description1: cyAs part of your application you’ll be asked to use your email address to set up an account. You will be able to use this email address and password to sign into other HMCTS services.
storingYourData4.description2: cyWe may ask for your permission to use your email address to send you emails using GOV.UK Notify. This system processes emails only within the European Economic Area until the point where emails are handed over to the email provider you use.
storingYourData4.description3: cyWe use cookies to collect data that tells us about how you’re using this service, including:

list.item1: cyif you open an email from us or click on a link in an email
list.item2: cyyour computer, phone or tablet’s IP address
list.item3: cythe region or town where you are using your computer, phone or tablet

storingYourData5.title: cyStoring your data
storingYourData5.description1: cyWhen you use this service you’ll be asked to use your email address to set up an account. You can use this email address and password to sign into other HMCTS services.

beforeYouSubmitYourInformation2.title: cyBefore you submit your information
beforeYouSubmitYourInformation2.description1: cyInformation you enter in the apply for probate service is saved until you decide to submit it. This allows you to save what you are doing and continue later. Saved information that you do not submit will be deleted after 180 days.

afterYouSubmitYourInformation2.title: cyAfter you submit your information
afterYouSubmitYourInformation2.description1: cyInformation you enter in the apply for probate service will be stored for 50 years and then deleted. Wills and grants of probate can be accessed as public records. Grants of probate do not include email addresses and telephone numbers, but they do include addresses.

sharingYourData4.title: cySharing your data
sharingYourData4.description1: cyWhile processing your application, another government department, agency or organisation might be involved and we may share your data with them.
sharingYourData4.description2: cyIf you contact us and ask for help with a service you are using, your personal data may be shared with the <a href="https://www.goodthingsfoundation.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" >Good Things Foundation (opens in a new window)</a >. This is a company who we have partnered with to offer face to face support.
sharingYourData4.description3: cyIn some circumstances we may share your data. For example, to prevent or detect crime, or to produce anonymised statistics.
sharingYourData4.description4: cyWe use Google Analytics to collect data about how a website is used. This anonymous data is shared with Google. Find out about this in our terms and conditions.
sharingYourData4.description5: cyStoring and sharing your data internationally
sharingYourData4.description6: cySometimes we need to send your personal information outside of the UK. When we do this we comply with data protection law.

usingTheFamilyPublicLawService.title: cyUsing the family public law service

whatIsThePersonalDataThatWe.title: cyWhat is the personal data that we collect
whatIsThePersonalDataThatWe.description1: cyWhen you use the Family Public Law service, we collect the following personal data:

list1.item1: cythe applicant's name, address, job role and contact details
list1.item2: cythe Local Authority solicitor's name, address and contact details
list1.item3: cythe social worker's name, address and contact details
list1.item4: cyname, date of birth, gender, and address of children in the case
list1.item5: cyname, date of birth, gender, address and contact details of respondents in the case
list1.item6: cyname, address and contact details of other parties in the case, for example witnesses
list1.item7: cydetails of any disability or litigation capacity (ability to understand proceedings) of any child, respondent or other party in the case
list1.item8: cydetails of other court cases respondents or children in the case have been involved in

list2.item1: cyinformation that tells us if you open an email from us, or click on a link in an email
list2.item2: cyinformation about how you use this service, like your IP address and the web browser you use. We do this by using cookies

whatWeDoWithYourData.title: cyWhat we do with your data
whatWeDoWithYourData.description2: cyPersonal data is processed by our staff in the UK and the data is stored in the UK.
whatWeDoWithYourData.description3: cyData relating to a case is stored until the youngest child reaches 18 years old, unless the case results in adoption where the data is stored for 100 years.
whatWeDoWithYourData.description4: cyWe use GOV.UK Notify to send emails. These are processed within the EEA until the point where emails are handed over to your email provider.

yourRights2.title: cyYour rights
yourRights2.description2: cyEmail data.access@justice.gov.uk if you want to see any of this information.

list.item1: cyto see the personal data that we hold on you
list.item2: cyto have the personal data corrected
list.item3: cyto have the personal data removed or deleted (this will depend on the circumstances, for example if you decide not to continue your claim or application)
list.item4: cythat access to the personal data is restricted (for example, you can ask to have your data stored for longer and not automatically deleted)

sharingYourData5.title: cySharing your data
sharingYourData5.description1: cyWe allow Google to use or share our website analytics data, find out about this in our  <a routerlink="/terms-and-conditions" href="/terms-and-conditions" >terms and conditions</a >.

receivingNotifications3.title: cyReceiving notifications
receivingNotifications3.description1: cyAs part of your application we will send you notifications to let you know how your application is proceeding.
receivingNotifications3.description2: cyEmail contactfpl@justice.gov.uk if you want to cancel email updates.

howToComplain2.title: cyHow to complain
howToComplain2.description1: cyIf you want to complain about how we have handled your personal data, email DataProtection@justice.gov.uk.
howToComplain2.description2: cyYou can complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office if you are unsatisfied with our response or believe we are not legally processing your personal data.

usingTheAppealAnImmigrationOrAsylum.title: cyUsing the Appeal an immigration or asylum decision service

thePersonalDataWeNeed4.title: cyThe personal data we need
thePersonalDataWeNeed4.description1: cyWhen you use the appeal an immigration or asylum decision service we ask for:

list.item4: cyyour email or mobile phone number
list.item7: cyinformation from the Home Office decision letter
list.item8: cyinformation on any support you need for a case management appointment or hearing, if you attend one

storingAndSharingYourData2.title: cyStoring and sharing your data
storingAndSharingYourData2.description1: cyYour data will be shared with the government department that made the decision you are appealing against. For example, the Ministry of Justice. This is so that the department can respond to your appeal.

afterYouSubmitYourInformation3.title: cyAfter you submit your information
afterYouSubmitYourInformation3.description1: cyThe information you submit will be deleted 2 years after the Tribunal has issued its decision and the last update has been made to your appeal.
afterYouSubmitYourInformation3.description2: cyIf the Tribunal doesn’t make a decision about your appeal (for example, it is withdrawn, or both parties agree) then the information you provide will be deleted 2 years after the appeal has been closed and the last update made.
afterYouSubmitYourInformation3.description3: cyIf you make a complaint against the Tribunal then information about the appeal is stored for 3 years after the last update on the complaint.

list1.item1: cyyour name or the name of your business or organisation
list1.item2: cyyour email or mobile phone number
list1.item4: cythe address of the property you are seeking possession of
list1.item5: cythe name of the person, business or organisation you are claiming against
list1.item7: cythe reasons you are making the claim
list1.item8: cyevidence you have to support your claim

thePersonalDataWeNeed5.description2: cyIf you are responding to a possession claim we ask you to check the personal information about you that was provided by the claimant which includes your name, your address and contact details.
thePersonalDataWeNeed5.description3: cyWe may ask you to provide:

list2.item2: cyyour business or organisation if you are acting on their behalf
list2.item3: cyyour response to the claim made against you
list2.item4: cyevidence you have to support your claim
